source_refs.note: Topic 3.2.1.2 (PDF 71-72, printed 68-69). The lock-code example is general and flagged.

items: The problem space is small, so it is feasible to generate and test every possible solution.
There is no clear strategy for finding a solution, so an exhaustive search is needed.
Heuristics or rules can reduce the number of generated solutions, making the process more efficient.

blocks.prompt: A 3-digit lock code can be found by trying 000 to 999. Why does generate and test suit this problem?
blocks.explanation: The space is small (1000 candidates) and each one is easy to test, so trying them all is feasible; a heuristic, such as trying likely codes first, can make it faster. This example is for illustration and is not from the book.

items: Use generate and test when the space is small, no better strategy exists, or heuristics can prune candidates.
